third_rejection.rejection: The dynamic odd/even SVEK port shield is correct for unstyled entry and exit points, but renderer dispatch rejects the same non-autarkic cluster as soon as qualified state paint or global shadowing is present. The generic fallback loses both EntityImageStateBorder paint and the cluster topology.

invariant: Java resolves state stereotypes in three independent stages. CommandCreateState maps only choice, fork, join, start, end, history, and history* case-insensitively to special leaf images. Entity.getEntityPosition maps only port and the entry, exit, pin, and expansion-position stereotypes away from NORMAL; Entity.isAutarkic tests that semantic position and cross-boundary links, not mere stereotype presence. EntityPosition then supplies the complete non-normal image model: entry and exit points are 12px circles, input and output pins are 12px squares, and top-to-bottom expansion inputs and outputs are 48x12 compartmented rectangles; only entry and exit points request Graphviz port P. EntityImageStateBorder paints every non-normal position and places its description outside the owning cluster. SvekNode first truncates the external-label width to an integer: widths at most 40 use a fixed 12px rectangle even though adjacent edges still name port P, while larger widths use a three-row HTML table whose fixed 12px middle cell defines P and whose spanning rows use fullWidth = max(10, floor(labelWidth) - 40). Under the pinned Graphviz 15 solver, that table is max(54, fullWidth + 16) by 36px and its centered P cell is max(12, (fullWidth + 24) / 3) by 12px. Dot ranks the reported table width with symmetric whole-point half-extents, giving a synthetic layout envelope of 2 * ceil(tableWidth / 2); this differs by one pixel when tableWidth is odd. EntityImageStateBorder paints the 12px symbol from the P cell's left edge, so its center is offset by 6 - portWidth / 2 from the solved node center. The extracted table and derivation are preserved in svek-port-shield-metrics.json. For an autarkic group, GroupMakerState still builds its autonomous image, and ordinary leaf descriptions remain part of EntityImageState content rather than invalidating autonomy. EntityImageStateCommon and InnerStateAutonom merge the base state/title/header/body signatures with the entity or group stereotype. Legacy StateAttributeFontName, StateAttributeFontSize, and StateAttributeFontStyle conversions feed the state title/header signatures as well as description text. ValueImpl.asFontFace recognizes exact bold, italic, plain/normal, or numeric-weight values; an unrecognized compound such as 'bold italic' resolves to the normal face. The merged font metrics determine each image dimension before SvekNode emits DOT dimensions, while merged fill, line, text, stroke, rounding, and shadow channels paint that same image. Explicit entity colors and strokes override merged style channels. An unmatched selector and an ordinary unmatched stereotype therefore leave geometry and paint unchanged.
causal_divergence: Rust preserves an ordinary stereotype string but originally rejected every stereotyped composite and every stereotyped child before autonomous layout, regardless of semantic entity position or image kind. It also accepted only nodesep and ranksep in the autonomous path, so any state style selector forced a different renderer even when the selector matched no entity. The first implementation corrected ordinary style resolution but retained three model gaps exposed by independent held-outs: it still rejected described autonomous leaves despite already sizing their descriptions; it substring-matched FontStyle and kept Font* ahead of AttributeFont* for title metrics, unlike Java's typed style conversion and state title/header signatures; and it excluded pin and expansion stereotypes from autonomy without carrying their semantic EntityPosition through the general cluster renderer, which then painted them as ordinary boxes. The second correction reproduced one 28px fullWidth shield observation as a constant 54x36 node with a 52/3px port and compared the untruncated floating label width directly with 40. Fresh checker inputs falsified both assumptions: a 40.2842px label remains on Java's basic branch, and independently longer labels change both solved node width and P-cell width. Replacing those guesses with dynamic formulas left one odd-width counterexample: Rust represented Java's reported 151px HTML node as a symmetric 75.5px fixed box, while dot ranks the HTML table with two 76px half-extents. The corrected shield then passed every unstyled heldout, but the non-autarkic renderer still rejected every non-empty skinparam set. A fresh diagram combining the same entry/exit topology with qualified paint and global shadowing therefore fell through to the generic renderer. Java keeps one SVEK graph: EntityImageStateBorder applies qualified fill, line, and text styles without shadow; RoundedContainer, ordinary EntityImageState, CircleStart, and CircleEnd apply inherited shadow; and LimitFinder extends only those shadowed rectangle/ellipse maxima by twice their style shadow delta.
planned_change: Recognize Java's reserved pseudostate stereotypes case-insensitively in the parser. Replace blanket stereotype rejection with a semantic autonomous-eligibility predicate: non-normal position stereotypes remain outside this autonomous renderer, while ordinary style stereotypes are eligible; specialized image decorations that Rust does not yet generate remain explicitly unsupported rather than silently painted as plain boxes. Resolve each ordinary state and composite from the diagram base style plus its matching stereotype-qualified state skinparams. Feed the resolved title and attribute font metrics into node and wrapper dimensions before layout, and use the same resolved fill, border, text, thickness, rounding, and shadow channels during emission, preserving explicit entity fill/stroke precedence. Preserve described ordinary leaves in autonomous images and emit their already-modelled attribute text below the divider. Mirror ValueImpl.asFontFace with exact-value parsing, and let qualified AttributeFont* properties override qualified Font* properties for the state title and description channels produced by Java's state title/header signatures. Introduce one semantic state-position classifier for entry, exit, input pin, output pin, expansion input, and expansion output stereotypes; use its Java dimensions, symbol, input/output cluster registration, label placement, and port-P behavior throughout the non-autarkic cluster renderer. Reproduce SvekNode's integer-truncated 40px entry/exit label threshold and fixed-rectangle short branch. For the long branch, derive fullWidth, reported table width, even-point layout envelope, dynamic P-cell width, and painted-symbol offset from the preserved Graphviz table model before routing and painted-frontier projection. Admit the same supported state style keys in the non-autarkic cluster path. Resolve qualified border-point fill, line, and text channels there, but do not shadow EntityImageStateBorder. Resolve inherited numeric/boolean shadowing for clusters, ordinary states, and start/end images; emit one source-seeded SVG shadow definition, attach it only to Java's shadowed primitives, reproduce RoundedContainer's separate shadow rectangle, and add twice the shadow delta only to those painters' LimitFinder maxima. Treat unmatched state selectors as inert for autonomous eligibility. Do not branch on fixture labels, special-case a stereotype merely because it appears in the golden corpus, or allow a visual value to alter geometry unless the corresponding Java style channel does.
